nodes.raw_latex:
\label{MLR}
	
	A $\mu_p$-ML-randomness test is a sequence $\{U^p_n\}_n$ that is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1(p)$ with $\mu(U^p_n)\le 2^{-n}$, where $2^{-n}$ may be replaced by any computable function that goes to zero effectively. 
	 
	A $\mu_p$-ML-randomness test is \emph{Hippocratic} if there is a $\Sigma^0_1$ class $S\subseteq 2^\omega\times\omega$ such that $S=\{(X,n):X\in U_n^p\}$. Thus, $U_n=U_n^p$ does not depend on $p$ and is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$.  
If $X$ passes all $\mu_p$-randomness tests then $X$ is \emph{$\mu_p$-random}. If $X$ passes all Hippocratic tests then $X$ is \emph{Hippocrates $\mu$-random}.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{is_test}
	
Consider a sequence $Y=\{Y_n\}_{n\in\omega}$ of independent Bernoulli($p$) random variables, with the sample average 
\[
\overline Y_n := \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} Y_i.
\]
Let $N(b)=2^{3b-1}$ and let 
\[
U_d=\bigcup_{b\ge d}\{Y: |\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|\ge 2^{-b}\}.
\]
Then $U_d$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1(p)$, and $\mu_p(U_d)\le 2^{-d}$, i.e., $\{U_d\}_{d\in\omega}$ is a $\mu_p$-ML-test.

The point is that the usual proof that each convergent sequence is Cauchy gives a $\Sigma^0_1$ class that has small $\mu_p$-measure for all $p$ simultaneously. Namely, let
\[
V_d:=\{Y: \exists a,b\ge d\,\,|\overline Y_{N(a)}-\overline Y_{N(b)}|\ge 2^{-a}+ 2^{-b}\}.
\]
Then $\{V_d\}_{d\in\omega}$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$. Recall from \Cref{is_test} that we defined
\[
U^{p}_d=\{Y:\exists b\ge d\,\, |\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|\ge 2^{-b}\}.
\]
If there is a $p$ such that $|\overline Y_{N(b)}-p|<2^{-b}$ for all $b\ge d$, then 
\[
|\overline Y_{N(a)}-\overline Y_{N(b)}|\le |\overline Y_{N(a)}-p|+|p-\overline Y_{N(b)}|< 2^{-a}+2^{-b}
\]
for all $a,b\ge d$; thus we have 
\[
V_d\subseteq \cap_{p} U^{p}_d
\]
and therefore 
\[
\mu_p(V_d)\le\mu_p(U^{p}_d)\le 2^{-d}
\]
for all $p$. 
 Thus if $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y\not\in V_d$ for some $d$. 

We next note that for any numbers $c> b$, 
\[
|\overline Y_{N(b)} - \overline Y_{N(c)}| < 2^{-b}+2^{-c} < 2^{-(b-1)},
\]
so $\{\overline Y_{N(c)}\}_{c\ge d}$ will remain within $2^{-(b-1)}$ of $\overline Y_{N(b)}$ for all $c>b$. That is, $\{\overline Y_{N(n)}\}_{n\ge d}$ is a Cauchy sequence (for each $b$ there is an $N(b)$ such that for all $n,m\ge N(b)$, $|\overline Y_n-\overline Y_m|\le 2^{-b}$) hence $q:=\lim_n \overline Y_{N(n)}$ exists. Write $q=.q_0q_1q_2\cdots$. Then
\[
|\overline Y_{N(b)}-q| <  2^{-(b-1)}, \text{ so }
\]
\[
|\overline Y_{N(b+1)}-q| <  2^{-b};
\]
if we define $\Theta_d$ as $\Psi_d$ in \Cref{random_computes} except with $N(\cdot)$ replaced by $N(\cdot+1)$, then
\[
q_n = \Theta_d^Y(n).
\] 
and so $Y$ computes $q$ using the Turing reduction $\Theta_d$.

Namely, let \[ V_d:=\Y: exists a,bge d\,\,|overline Y_N(a)-overline Y_N(b)|ge 2^-a+ 2^-b\. \] Then \V_d\_dinomega is uniformly Sigma^0_1. Recall from Crefis_test that we defined \[ U^p_d=\Y:exists bge d\,\, |overline Y_N(b)-p|ge 2^-b\. \] If there is a p such that |overline Y_N(b)-p|<2^-b for all bge d, then \[ |overline Y_N(a)-overline Y_N(b)|le |overline Y_N(a)-p|+|p-overline Y_N(b)|< 2^-a+2^-b \] for all a,bge d; thus we have \[ V_dsubseteq cap_p U^p_d \] and therefore \[ mu_p(V_d)lemu_p(U^p_d)le 2^-d \] for all p. Thus if Y is Hippocrates mu_p-random then Ynotin V_d for some d. We next note that for any numbers c> b, \[ |overline Y_N(b) - overline Y_N(c)| < 2^-b+2^-c < 2^-(b-1), \] so \overline Y_N(c)\_cge d will remain within 2^-(b-1) of overline Y_N(b) for all c>b. That is, \overline Y_N(n)\_nge d is a Cauchy sequence (for each b there is an N(b) such that for all n,mge N(b), |overline Y_n-overline Y_m|le 2^-b) hence q:=lim_n overline Y_N(n) exists. Write q=.q_0q_1q_2cdots. Then \[ |overline Y_N(b)-q| < 2^-(b-1), so \] \[ |overline Y_N(b+1)-q| < 2^-b; \] if we define Theta_d as Psi_d in Crefrandom_computes except with N(cdot) replaced by N(cdot+1), then \[ q_n = Theta_d^Y(n). \] and so Y computes q using the Turing reduction Theta_d.

Let \[ W_N:=\Y: exists nge N\,\,overline Y_nle q_1\cup\Y: exists nge N\,\,overline Y_nge q_2\ \] Then \W_N\_Ninomega is uniformly Sigma^0_1, and mu_p W_Nrightarrow 0 effectively: \[mu_p \Y: exists nge N\,\,overline Y_nle q_1\ le frac32(p-q_1)^4(N-1)\] Thus if Y is Hippocrates mu_p-random then Ynotincap_n W_n, i.e., overline Y_n is eventually always in the interval (q_1,q_2).
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $q_1$, $q_2$ be rational numbers with $q_1<p<q_2$.
Let
\[
W_N:=\{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\le q_1\}\cup\{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\ge q_2\}
\]
Then $\{W_N\}_{N\in\omega}$ is uniformly $\Sigma^0_1$, and $\mu_p W_N\rightarrow 0$ effectively:
\[\mu_p \{Y: \exists n\ge N\,\,\overline Y_n\le q_1\} \le \frac{3}{2(p-q_1)^4(N-1)}\]
Thus if $Y$ is Hippocrates $\mu_p$-random then $Y\not\in\cap_n W_n$, i.e., $\overline Y_n$ is eventually always in the interval $(q_1,q_2)$.
